title: Choose the visual world for setebaidservices.org (re-roll 1)
question: Steer honoured: big photographs of children at camp are the material in every card, and the flat two-ink print discipline you liked is kept as the print method of the lead. The roll assigned The Mailer. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Mailer
options.lineage: the tri-fold camp brochure that arrives in a Pennsylvania mailbox: full-colour photographs, two spot-colour inks, panels, creases, a tear-off reply card and the nonprofit postage indicia
options.thesis: The homepage is the brochure opened flat on the kitchen table: one big photograph per panel, one question per panel, and the reply card is the register link.
materials: two spot inks for everything printed over them
fold creases and a perforated reply card
options.viewport: Three panels edge to edge with faint creases between them. Left panel: one full-bleed photograph of a camper (a labelled placeholder until the real photos land), the camp name printed small at the top, and the season line printed across the bottom in the second ink: 'Summer 2027 registration is open. Late fee after May 15.' Centre panel: the hook in big first-ink type, 'Summer camp for kids who just happen to have diabetes', and under it three printed check-boxes with photo thumbnails: Ages 7 to 13 (HDYC), Ages 13 to 17 (Camp Setebaid), Families (Family Conference). Right panel: the ticked camp's card, July 11 to 17, 2027, Mifflinburg PA, 'Tier I to IV pricing: every family pays what it can, every child gets the same camp', and the Register link with Request info small beneath it. Ticking a box stamps it and reprints the right panel. On a phone the panels unfold one under the other, crease by crease.
options.risk: The most familiar artefact in this hand. Done timidly it is the category website with a paper texture. It only holds if the fold is real (panels, creases, the perforated reply card, the mailing panel as footer) and the photographs are big and real. The real photos are not in the repo yet, so every panel ships with a labelled placeholder until they arrive.

raised.raise: One photograph owns the cover panel at full bleed and nothing competes with it: no badge, no burst, no second image.
The three camp panels are identical modules, same anatomy every time (photo, ages, dates, cost, action), so a parent compares by sweeping across, never by opening one.
Two spot inks only, committed on every surface, with no gradients or tints beyond the halftone, and every motion holds a finished still under reduced motion.
One motion event per viewport, the fold opening, and the text stays readable all the way through it.

options.label: The Nightly Gallery
options.lineage: the daily photo gallery parents refresh every night of camp week, hoping to spot their own kid smiling
options.thesis: The photographs are the page. The homepage is a camp week seen the way parents actually see it: big pictures stamped by day and activity, newest first.
materials: a thin progress rule for Day 1 to Day 7
options.viewport: A wall of large photographs from one camp week fills the viewport, the newest at the top stamped 'Day 4, Tuesday, archery' (placeholders until the real photos land). The hook sits over the top photo in one line. A filter strip under it is the age picker: 'Show me: ages 7 to 13, ages 13 to 17, families', and picking one reorders the wall and pins that camp's dates, cost and register link at the top.
options.risk: Familiar: photo-grid websites are common, and this is where many runs in this category land. It depends entirely on a large supply of real photographs, which the repo does not have yet; with few photos it is thin. It also suggests campers' photos are public, so the privacy line must be explicit.

options.label: Teen-Magazine Quiz Spread
options.lineage: a nineties teen-magazine quiz over a torn-edge halftone photo collage with a verdict box at the fold
options.thesis: 'Which camp is yours?' as a one-question quiz over a collage of big halftone camp photographs; the verdict box is the camp, its dates, its cost and its register link.
materials: halftone photo blocks torn and taped
options.viewport: A spread of torn-edge camp photographs in halftone, the headline 'Which camp is yours?' at a tilt, one lettered row: A) my camper is 7 to 13, B) 13 to 17, C) we are a family. Circling an answer in gel-pen ink flips open the verdict box: HDYC or Camp Setebaid or the Family Conference with dates, tiers and Register.
options.case: Holds identification: today's parents of a 10-year-old were teens when these quizzes ran, and teens read the form instantly. Ties on clarity: the quiz is the age picker itself, but hot pink and acid green fight the calm a parent needs before trusting a medical team.
options.risk: Reads as a joke if the halftone and pen go too far; the medical-team panel needs a calm register the form does not naturally give.

options.label: Brick Build Instructions
options.lineage: a brick build-instruction book: numbered steps on sky-blue pages, 1:1 call-outs, wordless arrows
options.thesis: How camp works, step by step: 1 pick the camp, 2 register, 3 the deposit, 4 vaccinations, 5 packing list, 6 drop-off on July 11. The finished model on the box is a big photograph of camp.
materials: a photograph as the box-front picture
options.viewport: A box-front photograph of campers across the top, then the parts inventory: the two camps and the family conference as 1:1 call-outs with ages and dates. Step 1 is the age pick; the arrow shows where it seats. Each later step is a spread.
options.case: Holds identification: every parent of a 7 to 13-year-old has built one of these on the carpet. Loses clarity for this surface: numbered steps explain the process but not the place, and the photographs sit only on the box front.
options.risk: Strong for the 'before camp' checklist page, thinner as a homepage: a parent deciding whether to trust the camp is not yet ready for step 3.

options.label: Factory Records Sleeve
options.lineage: a matte black catalog sleeve with a white pulsar plot and colour-coded strips instead of words
options.thesis: Every artefact a numbered entry, names replaced by colour codes.
options.viewport: A black field, one white plot, a small catalog number.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no photographs, no names, nothing labelled twice. Parents do not identify with a record sleeve and the offer is hidden by design. It loses both axes.
options.kept: One image owns the field; vast unprinted ground.

options.label: VU-Meter Bridge
options.lineage: a row of ballistic VU needles across a recording desk
options.thesis: Identical meters read as one row; the room is read by sweeping.
options.viewport: Twenty meters shoulder to shoulder, needles leaning right together.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a meter for a children's camp reads as a blood-sugar gauge, the clinic you named as an anti-goal. No photographs. It loses both axes.
options.kept: Identical modules repeat as the row's ruler; compare by sweeping.
options.risk: A gauge on a page about kids.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.lineage: dense barcode columns and sine lattices strobing in pure black and white
options.viewport: A wall of hairline bars with a sine trace, snapping to negative.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no photographs, no warmth, and strobing is the opposite of a page for anxious parents. It loses both axes.
options.kept: Total two-value commitment; a still under reduced motion.

options.label: Alphabet Storm
options.lineage: letters condensing into words and breaking into weather
options.thesis: Language as matter; one word-weather event per viewport.
options.viewport: Black letters gather into a word and burst into rain across a white field.
options.case: Fuses poorly: surreal type weather has no photographs and no camp in it, and parents do not identify with it. It loses both axes.
options.kept: One motion event per viewport, text readable throughout.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The summer-camp website every camp ships: full-bleed photo of kids at the lake, a slogan, three cards, a quote, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: A full-bleed camp photo with the slogan and a Register button, then three cards: Camps, Donate, Volunteer.
canonCard.risk: Interchangeable with every other camp site by design, and the anti-goal you named.
